steps.say: Hypospadias is recognised at the first nappy change by three linked defects that always travel together. The urinary opening sits too far down the underside, the shaft bends downward with chordee, and the foreskin hoods over the top leaving the underside bare. Spotting the full triad matters because a lone low meatus without chordee is a different smaller operation.
steps.tx: Diagnose hypospadias by its **hypospadias triad** (three linked defects): proximal **ventral meatus** (low underside opening), ventral curvature called **chordee** (downward bend), and a hooded **dorsal prepuce** (top heavy foreskin with bare underside). The triad grades severity at a glance: distal holes with mild bend suit single stage repair, while proximal holes with severe bend demand staged reconstruction.

vis.alt: Illustration of penile examination findings including hypospadias meatus position.
vis.caption: Hypospadias on inspection: low ventral meatus with dorsal hooding. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The single most harmful act in hypospadias is a routine newborn circumcision done before the surgeon is consulted. The foreskin is not spare skin here but the measured graft bank for building the missing urethra, and once it is cut away the reconstruction loses its best material. Every birth attendant must leave the prepuce strictly alone when the meatus sits low.
steps.tx: Forbid neonatal cutting: **contraindication to circumcision** (never remove the foreskin) applies to every hypospadiac newborn, because **preputial skin** (foreskin tissue) is the measured graft bank for urethral reconstruction. A routine snip destroys dorsal hood flaps and inner preputial grafts, converting a one stage repair into a graft hunt, so counsel parents firmly and document the warning.

vis.alt: Operative drawing of circumcision sleeve resection technique.
vis.caption: Circumcision technique: strictly forbidden in hypospadias, the foreskin is graft material. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Timing is set by psychology as much as surgery: repair between 6 and 18 months, before the toddler forms genital awareness and lasting memory of operations. Operating in this window lets the child grow up with no recall of catheters and dressings, while tissues are supple and the penis still small enough for precise work. Late referrals still get fixed, but the anaesthetic and emotional bills run higher.
steps.tx: Schedule repair in the golden window: **repair timing** (operation calendar) between **6 and 18 months** (six to eighteen months) of age, the accepted **hypospadias age** (toddler repair period) before genital awareness and operative memory form. Early repair heals with supple tissues and no psychological imprint, while delayed surgery faces stiffer skin, bigger expectations, and school age embarrassment.

steps.say: The Snodgrass operation fixed more hypospadias worldwide than all other repairs combined, using nothing but the existing plate. A midline relaxing cut down the urethral plate lets its edges hinge open wide enough to roll into a tube without any graft, perfect for distal and mid shaft defects with a healthy supple plate. One incision converts a flat strip into a roofed neourethra.
steps.tx: Roll distal defects with **Snodgrass repair** (**TIP urethroplasty**, tubularized incised plate): a **midline relaxing incision** (central plate cut) hinges the urethral plate open for tension free tubularization without grafts. Ideal for distal and mid-shaft holes with a supple plate, TIP gives a slit-like meatus at the tip with minimal morbidity, so master this operation before attempting proximal monsters.

steps.say: When the plate is flat and stiff like cardboard, rolling fails and flipping succeeds. The Mathieu repair raises a perimeatal based skin flap from just below the hole and flips it upward over the defect like closing a book, suiting distal defects whose plate cannot tubularize. A rounder meatus is accepted in exchange for dependable healing on hostile tissue.
steps.tx: Flip stiff plates with **Mathieu repair** (flap turnover closure): a **perimeatal flap** (skin tongue hinged beside the hole) is raised from ventral shaft skin and flipped over the urethral defect. Choose Mathieu for distal holes with a flat non-pliable plate where TIP would stricture, accepting a rounder meatus in exchange for dependable healing on scarred ground.

steps.say: Severe proximal holes with a bent penis beyond 30 degrees after degloving defeat every one stage trick. The plate must be cut clean through to straighten the shaft, leaving a gap no tube can bridge at once, so the Bracka two stage repair grafts the raw bed with inner prepuce or buccal mucosa first and tubularizes it six months later. Staging converts a cripple into a straight organ.
steps.tx: Stage the severe end: **proximal hypospadias** (perineal and scrotal holes) with **chordee >30 degrees** (thirty degree bend after degloving) needs plate transection plus two-stage **Bracka technique** (graft then tube repair) using inner preputial or buccal graft. Stage one grafts the straightened bed, stage two rolls the matured graft into urethra, because forcing one stage on severe bend guarantees fistula and recurrent curve.

steps.say: The commonest heartbreak after hypospadias surgery is a pinhole leak along the suture line weeks later. Urethrocutaneous fistula strikes 5 to 15 percent of repairs where urine finds the skin through the closure, and the shield is a second waterproof layer: a vascularized dartos flap or tunica vaginalis blanket buried between neourethra and skin. Two layers were demonstrated to leak less than one.
steps.tx: Bury every repair under a second roof: **urethrocutaneous fistula** (urine leak to skin, **5% to 15%**, five to fifteen in a hundred) is the top complication, blocked by a **dartos barrier flap** (vascularized cover) of dartos or tunica vaginalis between tube and skin. The barrier layer waterproofs the closure, so harvest it routinely rather than explaining leaks to parents afterwards.

steps.say: A beautiful repair is ruined if the new opening scars shut, leaving the boy straining with a spray. Meatal stenosis creeps in when tubularization runs too far to the very tip or the distal closure strangulates, so the Snodgrass tube is deliberately stopped 2 to 3 millimetres short of the glans tip with a loose distal stitch. A wide open tip was designed to void freely and stay open.
steps.tx: Guarantee **meatal stenosis prevention** (keeping the tip open) by ending tubularization **2 mm to 3 mm** (two to three millimetres) proximal to the glans tip and avoiding distal overclosure (strangling tip stitches). The shortfall leaves a naturally wide meatus that voids in a straight stream, while tubes run to the very tip scar into pinholes needing lifelong dilatation.
